extracted.intended_audience: program sponsors, State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs), the Office of Apprenticeship (OA)/Registration Agencies, employers, apprentices, and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for implementing and operating registered apprenticeship and the new CTE apprenticeship model, including program registration, reviews, data reporting, wage rules, and other quality and procedural requirements; intended to inform stakeholders preparing comments and compliance plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program registration decision timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would require Registration Agencies to review CTE apprenticeship program registration applications and determine whether the program is eligible for registration within 90 days of receipt. Additionally, Registration Agencies would have to inform applicants in writing of decisions regarding program registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department estimates OA would register 41.8% of programs and SAAs 58.2%. The Department anticipates a GS-13 employee or State Training and Development Manager would spend 2 hours reviewing applications and informing applicants of decisions; seeks public comment on these time estimates and associated cost calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of completion credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration Agencies (OA and SAAs) must provide completion credentials/certificates to CTE apprentices upon program completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated burden for SAAs (Training and Development Manager) is 0.25 hour per certificate; Department multiplied number of apprentices by hour burden and wage to estimate costs; public comment requested on time/cost estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outreach, technical assistance, and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration Agencies would be required to provide outreach, technical assistance, and other support to potential sponsors to support adoption of registered CTE apprenticeship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department assumes OA will assist 41.8% of sponsors and SAAs 58.2%. Time estimated at 3 hours per assistance event by GS-13 or Training and Development Manager (State level), aligned with 2016 WIOA RIA; Department requests public comment on these estimates and cost calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program review frequency and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration Agencies must conduct reviews of registered CTE apprenticeship programs at least every 5 years. Reviews can be off-site (desk audits) or on-site workplace reviews and may include copying documents and interviews with employees, CTE apprentices, journeyworkers, supervisors, managers, and hiring officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department assumes 20% of sponsors are reviewed annually so all are reviewed over 5 years; OA and SAAs assumed to conduct assigned percentages of reviews. Estimated reviewer burden is 40 hours per review by a GS-13 or Training and Development Manager. Registration Agencies must provide a written Notice of Program Review Findings. Public comment sought on these assumptions and burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Program Review Findings and corrective actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a sponsor receives a Notice of Program Review Findings indicating failure of compliance, the sponsor must develop a compliance action plan or submit a written rebuttal to the Registration Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department estimates 20% of sponsors will be found noncompliant; estimated sponsor burden to develop a compliance action plan is 8 hours plus 0.17 hour to submit electronically (Training and Development Manager, private sector). Seeks comment on these assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for reconsideration process
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would allow sponsors to file a request for reconsideration if their initial application is denied, renewal is denied, or the program is deregistered; Registration Agencies must review the request and issue a written explanation of their final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department assumes 25% of sponsors will submit requests for reconsideration annually. Sponsor preparation burden estimated at 6 hours (Training and Development Manager, private sector). Registration Agency reviewer burden estimated at 2 hours (GS-13 or Training and Development Manager). Department requests comment on these estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data submission by apprentices
rubrics_metrics.description: CTE apprentices would be required to provide their information to program sponsors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department assumes apprentices spend 0.16 hour providing their information; cost estimates calculated by multiplying number of apprentices by hour burden and hourly wage. Seeks public comment on this estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor data compilation and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Program sponsors must compile and send to OA data on CTE apprentices, participating employers, and themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department assumes sponsors spend 0.167 hour (10 minutes) compiling and sending data on apprentices and participating employers and 0.67 hour compiling and sending data on themselves. Duties assumed performed by a Training and Development Manager (private sector); cost calculations provided and open for comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: OA compilation and public reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: OA must compile and develop reports based on submitted data to be made publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department assumes a GS-13 level employee will spend 60 hours compiling and developing reports; cost estimates provided. Department seeks comment on the time estimate and other aspects of public reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAAs compilation and reporting responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: CTE SAAs must compile and submit all CTE apprenticeship-related data and develop reports to be made publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department assumes management, computer systems, and administrative staff will spend 32, 240, and 72 hours, respectively, compiling and submitting data, and 40 hours compiling and developing reports. Cost estimates provided and consistent with registered apprenticeship assumptions; public comment requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to determine occupations suitable for apprenticeship
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would give the authority to determine occupations suitable for registered apprenticeship only to OA; occupations currently determined only by SAAs would need new requests to OA to continue being suitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change could impose a one-time cost to sponsors who must re-submit occupations; Department lacks data to quantify this cost and seeks comment and data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Off-the-job training documentation and minimum hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors would be required to submit documentation of the curriculum and number of off-the-job training hours, which cannot be less than 144 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs that do not meet the 144-hour minimum would need to update their off-the-job training requirements and submit documentation. Department does not have data on how many programs are affected and requests comments and data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension step prior to deregistration
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would add a suspension step prior to deregistration to allow sponsors time to update practices and achieve compliance without deregistration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SAAs and OA would need to develop suspension procedures and offer technical assistance; Department cannot quantify costs due to uncertainty about procedures and frequency, and notes potential for cost savings from fewer deregistrations. Requests comment on expected burdens and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Apprenticeship Council composition and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would establish requirements for State Apprenticeship Council composition, requiring councils to be composed of individuals familiar with occupations suitable for apprenticeship, registered apprenticeship programs, and opportunities across a wide range of industries and sectors, including employers, employer representatives, labor representatives, workforce board members, education system representatives, and other stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation is voluntary (de minimis costs to individuals), but SAAs would incur costs to recruit members and maintain the council; Department lacks data on burden/cost and seeks public comment and estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption provision for sponsors
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would provide relief to certain sponsors that can justify being exempt from certain requirements of subpart A of 29 CFR part 29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This could result in cost savings for sponsors and participating employers. Department is unable to project the number or nature of exemptions and seeks comment on how sponsors may use the exemption provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progressive wage increase requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would require a graduated schedule of increasing wages from entry wage to the journeyworker wage that includes at least one incremental wage step during the first 2,000 hours of on-the-job training and a final wage that is at least 75 percent of the journeyworker wage paid by the employer for that occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These changes would result in transfer payments from employers to apprentices where employers currently do not provide such increases; Department lacks data on prevalence and seeks comment on how progressive wage increases would impact apprentices and employers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on unreimbursed apprentice costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit the unreimbursed costs, expenses, and fees an apprentice may incur during the registered apprenticeship program to those that are necessary and reasonable and do not impose financial barriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to reduce excessive or unreasonable costs currently borne by some apprentices and shift costs toward sponsors/employers; Department lacks data on prevalence of excessive costs and requests comment and data.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-point assessments as a measure of quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would require end-point assessments (proposed §29.16) as a key method for sponsors to assess the skills and knowledge acquired by the apprentice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department considered alternatives (not requiring end-point assessments; conducting them every 2 years; requiring independent third parties to conduct them) but decided not to remove them because they help measure and ensure program quality. Department solicits comment on alternatives and cost/benefit tradeoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program review frequency alternatives and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Department analyzed regulatory alternatives for program review frequency: conducting reviews only for cause, every 2 years, or every 5 years (proposed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department rejected 'for cause only' because it could miss programs needing review; rejected every-2-years due to large cost increases and resource constraints; chose every-5-years as balance. Cost estimates for alternatives and assumptions (e.g., number of reviews, noncompliance rate) are provided and open to comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of non-compete provisions and complaint process improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would remove non-compete provisions and improve the complaint process as part of quality improvements to advance worker rights and equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These reforms are characterized as likely to improve worker mobility, economic outcomes, and equity, especially for underserved communities; Department describes expected distributional impacts and requests comment on effects.
